title: Matched Allen slice data leave decay-time matching between convergent excitatory and inhibitory inputs uncertain
abstract: We tested whether excitatory and inhibitory inputs to one neuron have closer voltage-response decay times than matched inputs to different neurons. We used the Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small database. We fixed recording and source and target cell labels. The score was the best normalized residual energy between two ideal exponential decay tails. In mouse visual cortex, 21 convergent and 24 disjoint pairs from 13 inferred donors gave a difference of 0.0061. The nominal 97.5% donor bootstrap interval was -0.0896 to 0.1242. Negative differences mean closer matching at a shared target. Human temporal cortex had only two inferred donors and a difference of -0.0056. Mouse distance matching and removal of endpoint decay values left intervals that included zero. The human result changed direction after endpoint removal. The data do not resolve a shared-target matching benefit. Small selected samples, missing labels, fit uncertainty, inferred donors, and membrane-state differences limit inference. The score describes decay mismatch under a linear tail model, not measured physiological cancellation. The package supplies code, edge and motif tables, checks, and a figure.

display.caption: Decay mismatch at a shared target minus matched four-cell controls. Negative values favor closer matching. Intervals are nominal 97.5% donor bootstrap intervals; fewer than two donors give no plotted estimate. Human intervals with two donors have very low resolution.

Published same-type timing comparison supplied shared-versus-disjoint matching and donor grouping precedents. This work adds cross-type E/I convergence and a bounded decay mismatch score; no code or tables were reused.
